definition: The turning point of a parabola, which lies on its axis of symmetry: a minimum point when the parabola opens upwards ($a > 0$ in $y = ax^{2} + bx + c$) and a maximum point when it opens downwards ($a < 0$).
A line that a graph can be folded along so the two halves match; for the parabola $y = ax^{2} + bx + c$ it is the vertical line $x = -\frac{b}{2a}$ through the vertex.
A point on a graph that is at least as high as every point near it; it need not give the greatest value on the domain, which may be at an end point.
A point on a graph that is at least as low as every point near it; it need not give the least value on the domain, which may be at an end point.

A straight line that a graph gets closer and closer to as $x$ or $y$ grows without limit, written as an equation such as $x = 3$ (vertical) or $y = 2$ (horizontal); a graph may cross a horizontal asymptote at a finite value of $x$.
